name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent
operator: GitHub (the vendor); each organisation is the operator of its own deployment
what: The asynchronous agent on GitHub.com that creates branches, writes code and opens pull requests in response to assigned issues.
note: An example scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar; the closest published shape, a hosted Actions runner with no agent, is not the same thing.

I04.n: It writes code in an "ephemeral, firewalled environment".

I08.n: It "can create branches, write code, and open pull requests in response to assigned issues".

I10.n: Repositories, issues and pull requests across one organisation.

I11.n: It "can receive information and context from MCP" and from external applications.

I18.n: The person assigns a task and reviews the pull request before merging.

I20.n: The vendor states intended uses: maintenance, feature development, prototyping.

I21.n: "It can only push to a single branch"; it has no access to Actions secrets beyond those configured for it.
I21.span: It can only push to a single branch

I22.n: The page lists limitations: limited scope, inaccurate code, security risks, public code matches.

I25.n: Read-only where the user has only read access; one branch to push to.

I27.n: Its commits are signed and show as Verified.

I38.n: Workflows triggered by its pull requests "require approval from a user with write access before they will run".
I38.span: require approval from a user with write access before they will run

I41.n: Commits are authored by Copilot with the person as co-author; matches are shown in the agent session logs.

I45.n: "By default, Copilot’s access to the internet is limited by a firewall." The vendor adds that it "should not be considered a comprehensive security solution".
I45.span: access to the internet is limited by a firewall

I56.n: Its commits and pull requests are attributed to Copilot.

S2.n: A registry lists servers that partners and the community publish for it.
S2.span: a curated list of MCP servers from partners and the community

S3.n: The documentation publishes an llms.txt index.

I14.n: The vendor publishes and maintains a Model Context Protocol server for its platform.

not_credited.what: New code is analysed with CodeQL, secret scanning and dependency analysis during generation.
not_credited.why: That tests what the agent produces. No indicator asks for it yet, and it is not evidence that the agent itself is tested.

configurations.name: As shipped
configurations.note: The firewall and its recommended allowlist are on.

configurations.name: With external tools connected
configurations.note: Model Context Protocol servers and other applications.

moved: As above. Scanning of generated code is no longer counted as testing of the agent.

review.note: Published as an example on 10 November 2026, before the review workflow existed. Mapped by one agent. It goes through two rounds of review next.
